title: The Circumgalactic Medium: Absorption, Cooling and Baryon Budgets Against Published Survey Values

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Chiara Papadopoulos, and this is The Circumgalactic Medium: Absorption, Cooling and Baryon Budgets Against Published Survey Values. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Chiara Papadopoulos, and this is The Circumgalactic Medium: Absorption, Cooling and Baryon Budgets Against Published Survey Values. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “COS-Dwarfs: Carbon Absorption, Covering Fractions and a Reservoir Outweighing Its Galaxy”. Its stated result is: Headline result: dwarfs cool mass 1e9 msun dwarfs = 2.228; dwarfs reservoir to stellar ratio dwarfs = 2.228; dwarfs covering strong cii dwarfs = 0.4; dwarfs halo allowance 1e9 msun dwarfs = 15.7; dwarfs cool share allowance percent dwarfs = 14.19; dwarfs metal mass 1e6 msun dwarfs = 4.457 Operating (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'COS-Dwarfs: Carbon Absorption, Covering Fractions and a Reservoir Outweighing Its Galaxy'; 'COS-Halos Cool Gas: Neutral Column, Covering Fraction and the Cool Mass Inside 160 Kiloparsecs'; 'COS-Halos O VI: Column Density, Ionisation Correction and the Warm-Hot Gas Mass'; 'Circumgalactic Pressure and Density: A Power-Law Profile Weighed and Checked for Hydrostatic Support'; 'Closing the L-Star Baryon Census: Stars, Disc Gas and Three Halo Phases Against the Cosmic Allowance'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'COS-Dwarfs: Carbon Absorption, Covering Fractions and a Reservoir Outweighing Its Galaxy'. The result it reported gives a value for mass 1e9 msun dwarfs, and that value is what this question asks for.

Find mass 1e9 msun dwarfs in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'COS-Dwarfs: Carbon Absorption, Covering Fractions and a Reservoir Outweighing Its Galaxy' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: mass 1e9 msun dwarfs = 2.228; covering strong cii dwarfs = 0.4; allowance 1e9 msun dwarfs = 15.7. (3) This question asks for the value paired with mass 1e9 msun dwarfs. (4) In that row, mass 1e9 msun dwarfs stands beside 2.228 — so the answer the lesson gives is 2.228. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.

questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
